setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Git responds with a version number

setupSteps.title: Install Node LTS
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Node responds with a version number

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.body: Keep it open beside Iris.
steps.verifierLabel: Terminal is open

steps.title: Check Git and Node
steps.body: Use Terminal. Git and the current Node LTS are required.
steps.verifierLabel: Git and Node respond with version numbers

hints: No version for git? Run xcode-select --install and let Apple's installer finish.
Node missing? Install the LTS from nodejs.org, then open a fresh Terminal window.

steps.title: Install pnpm
steps.body: The interface is a pnpm project.
steps.verifierLabel: pnpm responds with a version number

expect.prompt: In the shell, has `npm install -g pnpm` finished — a summary line such as "added 1 package" or "changed 1 package", with the prompt back and no error? Answer not done while it is still downloading, or if it stopped on a permissions error such as EACCES.

hints: If npm reported a permissions error, install Node from nodejs.org rather than a system package manager.
Command finished but nothing found? Open a fresh Terminal window so the new PATH is picked up.

steps.title: Install Rust
steps.body: Run the single command the page shows, then reopen Terminal.
steps.verifierLabel: cargo responds with a version number

expect.prompt: In the terminal, has the rustup installer finished — a line such as "Rust is installed now. Great!", with the prompt back and no error? Answer not done while it is still downloading or still asking which installation option to use.

hints: Paste the command rustup.rs shows into Terminal and take the default install.
Already finished? Open a new Terminal window — cargo only joins the PATH of new shells.

steps.title: Install CMake
steps.body: Already have cmake? This is already done. The speech engine needs it to build.
steps.verifierLabel: cmake responds with a version number

point.descriptor: the macOS universal .dmg row in the download table

hints: Already have cmake? This step finishes the moment it answers.
Installed from the .dmg? Drag CMake to Applications, then run its "Install Command Line Tools" item so cmake joins your PATH.

steps.title: Copy WhimprFlow to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d WhimprFlow/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/WhimprFlow.git
fi
steps.verifierLabel: A WhimprFlow folder appears

hints: If it stopped partway, delete the WhimprFlow folder and run the command again.
Permission denied? Run it from your home folder rather than a synced or network drive.

steps.title: Open the WhimprFlow folder
steps.verifierLabel: Your terminal prompt is inside the WhimprFlow folder

steps.title: Use the reviewed version
steps.verifierLabel: Git reports the reviewed commit

steps.title: Install the interface packages
steps.body: The last line fixes a pnpm build-approval quirk — it's a no-op when not needed.
steps.command:
cd ui
pnpm install
cd ..
pnpm --dir ui approve-builds --all || true
steps.verifierLabel: The install finishes without an error

steps.title: Make the speech model folder
steps.body: The model is too large to ship in the repository.
steps.verifierLabel: The models folder exists

steps.title: Download the speech model
steps.body: About 150MB — Iris fetches it straight into the models folder.
steps.verifierLabel: ggml-base.en.bin sits in the models folder

steps.title: Build the app
steps.body: The first build compiles Whisper, so it takes a while.
steps.verifierLabel: A WhimprFlow.app appears in the bundle folder

steps.title: Put WhimprFlow in Applications
steps.body: Copy the freshly built app into Applications so it's a real, launchable Mac app.
steps.verifierLabel: WhimprFlow.app is in your Applications folder

steps.title: Open WhimprFlow
steps.body: Launch it to finish setup — and so it shows up in your apps list.
steps.verifierLabel: WhimprFlow opens

steps.title: Choose how speech is cleaned up
steps.body: In Settings pick OpenAI and paste a key, or keep the raw transcript.
steps.verifierLabel: Settings saves without an error

hints: Staying on raw or local? Nothing to paste — move on once Settings has saved.
Pasted a key and nothing changed? Press Save beside the field rather than Enter.

steps.title: Grant Accessibility
steps.body: Press Grant on the Accessibility row and allow WhimprFlow. The row goes green on its own.
steps.verifierLabel: The Accessibility row reads Granted

point.descriptor: the Grant button next to Accessibility in the Set up WhimprFlow window

hints: The row goes green by itself — there is no need to quit WhimprFlow or toggle it off and on.
Nothing happening after you allowed it? Check you allowed WhimprFlow rather than Terminal in the list.

steps.title: Grant the microphone
steps.body: Press Grant on the Microphone row and allow it. WhimprFlow needs it to hear you.
steps.verifierLabel: The button at the bottom reads Enter WhimprFlow

point.descriptor: the Grant button next to Microphone in the Set up WhimprFlow window

hints: Grant greyed out? Do the Accessibility row first — the microphone unlocks after it.
If the row says macOS is judging this as Terminal, quit WhimprFlow and open it from Applications so it asks for itself.
Input Monitoring is the third row and is optional — you can enter without it.

steps.title: Hold Fn and speak
steps.body: Release the key and your words land where the cursor is.
steps.verifierLabel: Clean text appears in the app you were typing in

steps.title: Install Rust

hints: Run the downloaded rustup-init.exe and take the default install.
Already finished? Close PowerShell and open a new window so cargo is on the PATH.

steps.title: Install the C++ build tools
steps.body: Tick Desktop development with C++, then install.
steps.verifierLabel: The installer reports it finished

point.descriptor: the Desktop development with C++ workload tile

steps.title: Install CMake
steps.body: Pick the Windows x64 installer and let it add CMake to PATH.
steps.verifierLabel: cmake responds with a version number

point.descriptor: the Windows x64 Installer row ending in .msi

steps.title: Install LLVM
steps.body: Set LIBCLANG_PATH to its bin folder if the build cannot find it.
steps.verifierLabel: LLVM is installed

point.descriptor: the LLVM win64.exe installer under Assets on the newest release
